newsitem.title: USA: CBOT expands limits, margins for soybean complex.
newsitem.headline: CBOT expands limits, margins for soybean complex.

text.p: Chicago Board of Trade soybean, soymeal and soyoil markets will trade with expanded margin requirements and on expanded daily limits beginning Monday following limit-up closes Friday, the exchange said.
The expanded limit for soybeans will be 45 cents per bushel, the limit for soymeal will be $15.00 per ton, and the limit for soyoil will be 1.50 cents per pound, the CBOT said.
The initial margin requirement for soybeans was raised to $2,025 from $1,350, and maintenance and hedge margins were raised to $1,500 from $1,000, according to the exchange.
The initial margin requirement for soybean meal was raised to $1,215 from $810, and hedge and maintenance margins will go to $900 from $600.
In soyoil, the exchange raised the initial margin requirement to $810 from $540, and the maintenance requirement was raised to $600 from $400, exchange officials said.
The changes will be in place for two business days.
